## The problem the project addressed

National evidence can lose locally important spatial and governance detail when it is scaled for place-based climate-impact assessment.

How can national evidence be scaled for local climate-impact assessment without obscuring information that matters to local decisions?

## What the project produced

The completed project examined data-scaling methods and their implications through verified institutional project material and a connected scholarly publication.

## What it helps us understand

The work helps researchers and practitioners inspect how scale and spatial resolution shape the impacts and governance implications visible in local appraisal.

## Limits and context

Completed foundational prior work with an authoritative institutional project record.

**What not to infer.** The project does not establish one universally valid data-scaling method.

## Outputs and tools

- [Data Scaling: Implications for Climate Action and Governance in the UK](/publications/data-scaling-climate-action-governance-uk.html)
